transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

It sounds frustrating to keep emptying a container that is already empty. This usually happens for one of three reasons: 1) The container isn't pushed in quite firmly enough (it needs to click), 2) The small float inside the container is stuck or the lid isn't sealing properly, or 3) There is a blockage preventing water from reaching the sensor correctly. To help narrow this down, could you please check the rating plate inside the door opening and tell me the full model number (it usually starts with WTW, WDU or similar)? This will help us identify exactly how your specific Bosch dryer handles the water.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The container clicks in fine, I've checked that. The full model number is on the back and I can't get to it as the dryer is stacked on the washer. All I know is the manual says it starts WTG8.

Since the container clicks in firmly but the light stays on even though it's empty, the most common cause is that the small float inside the container itself is stuck. This float tells the machine when the tank is full; if it gets stuck in the 'full' position (often due to lint or detergent residue), the dryer thinks the tank is full and stops. Please take the water container out again and check that the small plastic float at the bottom moves freely up and down. If it feels stiff or won't move, gently clean around it with a bit of warm soapy water and a cloth to ensure it slides easily. Let me know if you find it stuck.
I'm not sure which float you mean, I can't really tell what's in there. The container is nearly empty anyway, so surely it can't be thinking it's full?

[Heading: Likely cause: float switch]
Since the container clicks in firmly but the light stays on even though it's empty, and we can't easily see inside to check a specific float, the issue is likely that the sensor itself (the water level switch) or the control board is faulty. It is telling the machine the tank is full when it isn't. As this requires internal diagnosis and part replacement beyond basic owner checks, I recommend calling an engineer.
